item.title: Lions Club Eyeglass Collection Drive
item.description:
The Oxford Lions Club is collecting used eyeglasses, sunglasses, and cases to donate to children in need worldwide. Donated glasses are modified to meet individual children's vision needs—the club sends over 900 pairs annually. Donations due by mid-May can be sent to Betsy Beaton (Marshall Elementary School) or Shaunna Tafelski (Board Office), with pickup available upon request.

item.title: Every Kid Healthy Week Activities
item.description:
Action for Healthy Kids presents Every Kid Healthy Week from April 20th-24th with daily themed activities: - Mindfulness Monday (April 20): Journaling, deep breathing, and sharing gratitude - Tasty Tuesday (April 21): Try new foods, help prepare meals, have an indoor picnic - Wellness Wednesday (April 22): Go for a walk, play outdoor games, have a dance party - Tech-Free Thursday (April 23): Device-free meals, turn off electronics for 1 hour for reading/arts/games - Family Friday (April 24): Pick a family activity and share appreciation for each family member

Families are encouraged to take pictures participating in activities and post on social media with #HealthyLikeRox.

item.description:
The PAX Good Behavior Game is a research-based classroom strategy that helps students make positive choices and collaborate with others. It promotes a calmer, more focused learning environment through kindness, teamwork, and respectful behavior.

item.title: Allergies or Cold: Know the Difference
item.description:
The school nurse provides a flowchart to help distinguish between allergy symptoms and cold symptoms. Key differences: Allergies typically involve clear mucus, seasonal occurrence, itchiness, and symptoms that last for extended periods. Colds usually present with green or yellow mucus, fever, body discomfort, and symptoms that come on quickly and taper off fairly rapidly. Call your doctor if symptoms last longer than two weeks, symptoms worsen or new symptoms develop, you have a sore throat or fever higher than 100 degrees for longer than three days, or you experience intense chest pain and shortness of breath.

item.title: Allergies or Cold Decision Guide
item.description:
The school nurse provides a visual flowchart to help determine whether symptoms indicate allergies or a cold. Key differences: allergies typically cause itchy eyes/nose/throat, clear mucus, and symptoms that occur seasonally or persist for extended periods; colds typically cause green/yellow mucus, body discomfort, fever, and symptoms that come on fast and taper off quickly. Call your doctor if symptoms last longer than two weeks, worsen or new symptoms develop, you have a sore throat or fever higher than 100 degrees for longer than three days, or you experience intense chest pain and shortness of breath.

item.title: Allergies or Cold: Know the Difference
item.description:
The school nurse provides a diagnostic flowchart to help distinguish between allergies and a cold. Key differentiators include: - Mucus color: Clear mucus suggests allergies; green or yellow suggests a cold - Symptom duration: Seasonal or extended symptoms indicate allergies; quick onset and resolution suggests a cold - Itchiness: Itchy eyes, nose, and throat are more common with allergies - Fever: Having a fever points toward a cold rather than allergies

Call your doctor if symptoms last longer than two weeks, worsen, include sore throat/fever over 100°F for more than three days, or involve intense chest pain and shortness of breath.

item.title: Spring State Testing Approaches for Grades 3-5
item.description:
Ohio State Testing for 3rd-5th graders is coming soon. Teachers will share specific testing dates with families. Please avoid scheduling appointments during testing times to ensure students can participate. A testing assembly will be held to share tips and encourage students. Five tips for testing success include: get plenty of rest, be on time, eat a good breakfast, relax and take deep breaths, and follow your teacher's directions.

item.title: The Parent Project Program for Parents and Teens
item.description:
The Parent Project is a free 10-week program for Butler County residents that empowers parents and transforms teens through the Why Try Program. The program runs Tuesdays, April 14 - June 16, 6pm-8pm via Zoom and helps parents learn to never argue with teens, prevent/intervene in alcohol or drug use, improve school attendance and performance, and explore solutions for media issues. The program uses visual metaphors to teach social, emotional, and leadership principles with a multisensory approach for every learning type. Contact Patsy Bolden at pbolden@ccswoh.org / 513-867-7072 for more information. (Syllabus fee $10.61 for out-of-county residents)
